title: How do you build a training matrix for a security company?
seoTitle: Training matrix for a security company
description: Build a security company training matrix: license classes, first aid, refreshers, use of force and venue add-ons for guards, crowd controllers and operators.
shortAnswer: A security company training matrix is built by listing each license class or specialty the company deploys, such as unarmed guard, crowd controller, bodyguard, cash-in-transit guard, dog handler, armed guard and monitoring center operator, against the qualification, first aid, refresher and site specific duties each market attaches to it. Every cell records the deadline, whether the rule or the company set it, and the certificate or record a licensing police unit would inspect.
keyTakeaways: In security, the license is the training gate: NSW, Victoria, California and Portugal all make specified courses a condition of working, so the matrix doubles as a deployability register.
Rows should follow license subclasses and specialties, because each one adds units, permits or refresher hours on top of the base course.

Several clocks are fixed: NSW first aid every three years, California's 8 hours of annual continuing training, Portugal's five year card with a refresher course, and Victoria's refresher within 12 months before renewal from 5 October 2026.
Guards placed at licensed venues pick up the venue's rules: in NSW, security staff monitoring patrons need Responsible Service of Alcohol training.

Employers hold part of the evidence burden. California employers keep guard training records for the duration of employment, and NSW master licensees must ensure the operatives they supply hold current first aid.

sections.heading: Why is a security company matrix also a deployment register?

blocks.text: Because in private security a lapsed course usually means a lapsed license, and an unlicensed operative cannot lawfully be rostered. Licensing units in NSW, Victoria, California and Portugal tie the right to work to completing approved training, so the matrix answers a scheduling question as well as a compliance one: who can be sent to which site today.

The general approach in [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) applies, with one change in emphasis. A security matrix records the license number, class and expiry next to every training cell, and it adds a site column, because the same guard can need extra training when deployed to a licensed venue. Treating it as a [skills matrix](/glossary/skills-matrix) with legal status attached is closer to the truth than treating it as a course list.

sections.heading: Which license classes and specialties should be the rows?

blocks.text: Use the license subclasses and specialties the regulators define, since each one carries its own course, permit or refresher. The table shows the rows most operators need.

sections.heading: What does each market require of security staff?

blocks.text: Columns come from the regulation pages for each market where the company deploys staff. The summaries below use only what those pages record.

items: **New South Wales.** Class 1 has six subclasses. Applicants for every subclass except 1E pass the SLED Pre-Enrolment Assessment, complete the NSW Security Licence Course with a SLED Approved Organisation based on CPP20218 units, and hold a first aid certificate issued within three years (HLTAID011 for 1A and 1C, HLTAID014 for 1B, 1D and 1F) that must be renewed every three years. Master licensees must ensure the Class 1 operatives they provide, except 1E, hold current first aid ([NSW security licence](/regulations/nsw-security-licence-training-requirements)).

**Victoria.** Applicants complete the approved qualification for each activity with an approved RTO within 12 months of applying, for example CPP20218 for unarmed guards and crowd controllers. From 5 October 2026, renewing individual operators must also complete HLTAID011, and guards, crowd controllers and bodyguards must complete the approved online refresher within 12 months before renewal ([Victorian private security](/regulations/victoria-private-security-licence-training)).

**California.** Guards complete 8 hours of Power to Arrest and Appropriate Use of Force training before registration, with the exam passed at 100%, then 32 hours of skills training within six months and 8 hours of continuing training every year, at least 2 of which review use of force ([California security guard](/regulations/california-security-guard-training-requirements)). As California employers, security firms also fall under Labor Code section 6401.9, which requires workplace violence prevention training when the plan is first established and annually after that ([California workplace violence prevention](/regulations/california-workplace-violence-prevention-training)).

**Portugal.** Under Law 34/2013 as republished by Law 46/2019, staff must pass approved courses and hold a PSP professional card valid for five years; renewal requires a refresher course. Ordinance 148/2014 sets minimum refresher hours by specialty, from 10 hours for alarm center operators to 60 hours for close protection officers ([Portugal private security](/regulations/portugal-private-security-training-requirements)).

**Australia, first aid generally.** Where the model WHS laws apply, the Code of Practice recommends CPR refresher training every year and requalification every three years ([first aid in Australia](/regulations/first-aid-training-requirements-australia)). Victoria's compliance code takes the same approach to CPR and requalification.

**Venue deployments in NSW.** Security staff and crowd controllers monitoring patron behavior must hold Responsible Service of Alcohol training on an NSW competency card valid for five years ([NSW RSA](/regulations/responsible-service-of-alcohol-training-nsw)). At gaming venues, Liquor & Gaming NSW does not recommend security officers as Responsible Gambling Officers ([NSW RCG](/regulations/nsw-responsible-conduct-of-gambling-training)).

sections.heading: Which security training intervals are set by regulators?

blocks.text: More than in most industries: security regulators commonly set hours and cycles outright. The matrix should still mark which intervals came from a rule and which from the company, so an auditor can see the difference at a glance.

items: **Set by rule.** NSW first aid renewal every three years; California 32 hours within six months and 8 hours each year; Victorian refresher within 12 months before renewal; Portugal refresher on card renewal or where the last training was over five years ago; NSW RSA every five years.

**Set by license term.** NSW licenses can be renewed up to eight weeks before expiry and, after 90 days past expiry, a new application with current course evidence is needed. Victorian renewal applications are sent 10 weeks before expiry.

**Chosen by the company.** Site inductions, post orders, client procedures and monitoring center refreshers are rarely set by the license rules covered here. Pick an interval, record the reason, and see [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

**Workplace safety duties.** The Australian first aid Code recommends annual CPR refreshers; a company that rosters lone night patrols may decide that every guard, not only designated first aiders, should hold it.

sections.heading: What evidence do licensing police and clients expect?

blocks.text: Expect requests for certificates with issue dates, provider identity and license linkage, because licensing units check that training came from an approved organization within the permitted window. Clients increasingly ask for the same evidence before they accept a guard on site.

items: **Approved provider proof.** NSW accepts only SLED Approved Organisation training, and Victoria requires an approved RTO with training valid within 12 months of the application.

**Certificate retention.** In California, guards keep certificates until their registration expires or is canceled, employers keep records for the duration of employment, and providers retain certificates for at least two years.
**Shift records.** NSW requires sign-on registers each shift, which link a deployed operative to a date and site and so to the training that was current at that time.

**Penalty exposure.** NSW sets maximum fines of $5,500 for security activity without a license, and Portugal classes some breaches as very serious offenses with fines for legal persons up to EUR 44,500. The guide on [preparing training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) explains how to keep the file ready.

sections.heading: Which security training changes should be in the matrix now?

blocks.text: Two jurisdictions have rules in motion as at November 2026. Add them as dated rows so status changes on the right day.

items: **19 June 2025, Victoria:** most changes under the Private Security and County Court Amendment Act 2024 commenced, removing classes A and B and defining seven activities.
**19 December 2025, Victoria:** independent contractors with an ABN need both a business and an individual license (investigators excepted).
**5 October 2026, Victoria:** renewing operators must complete HLTAID011 first aid and, for guards, crowd controllers and bodyguards, the approved refresher within 12 months before renewal.

**31 December 2026, California:** the Occupational Safety and Health Standards Board is required to adopt a general industry workplace violence standard; an advisory meeting on the draft title 8 section 3343 was held on 27 October 2026.

blocks.title: Watch item
blocks.text: The OSHSB proposed regulations list for October 2026 showed no workplace violence rulemaking notice. Keep the California standard as a watch item until a formal proposal appears, and continue training under Labor Code section 6401.9.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each license class and site requirement to the learning outcomes and assessment points that prove competence, so a security company can show which course satisfies which licensing condition in each market. When a regulator changes renewal conditions, the affected roles and evidence rules are flagged. See [operational procedures programs](/programs/operational-procedures).

faqs.q: Can one base course cover guards in NSW and Victoria?
faqs.a: Both jurisdictions build on CPP20218 Certificate II in Security Operations for unarmed work, but delivery rules differ. NSW accepts only SLED Approved Organisation training after a Pre-Enrolment Assessment, while Victoria requires an approved RTO and training completed within 12 months of the application. Interstate holders may apply under mutual recognition for equivalent activities only.

faqs.q: Do monitoring center operators need the same training as guards?
faqs.a: Not in every market. NSW Class 1E applicants need no formal training, and Victorian holders licensed only as monitoring center operators are exempt from the new refresher. Portugal still sets 10 refresher hours for alarm center operators. Give the role its own row rather than copying the guard requirements.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for first aid certificates of supplied staff in NSW?
faqs.a: Master license holders must ensure the Class 1 operatives they provide, except 1E, hold a current first aid certificate. The certificate must also be renewed every three years for license purposes, so the matrix should alert both the operative and the supplying company before expiry.

faqs.q: Should armed guards have separate rows?
faqs.a: Yes. In NSW, 1F applicants complete additional units followed by Security Firearms Training and a Category H Provisional Pistol Licence, and Victoria trains armed guards through a separate CPP31318 stream. Neither requirement applies to unarmed staff, so merging the rows would either overtrain guards or hide a firearms gap.

factCheck.claim: Class 1 has six subclasses: 1A Security Officer, 1B Bodyguard, 1C Cash-in-Transit Guard, 1D Guard Dog Handler, 1E Monitoring Centre Operator, 1F Armed Guard; a person can hold more than one.

Class 1 applicants except 1E must complete the SLED Pre-Enrolment Assessment including an LLN test, a first aid certificate issued within three years (HLTAID011 for 1A and 1C, HLTAID014 for 1B, 1D, 1F), and the CPP20218 mandatory units; first aid must be renewed every three years; only SLED Approved Organisation training accepted; 1E, 2B and 2C need no formal training.

Additional units: 1B CPPSEC3122 and 3123; 1C CPPSEC3118, 3119, 3120; 1D CPPSEC3112 and 3113; 1F CPPSEC3101, 3102, 3103 followed by Security Firearms Training and a Category H Provisional Pistol Licence. 2A requires CPP41519 and five years experience; 2D requires a TAE Certificate IV and three years experience; 2E requires CPP30619.
Renewal online up to eight weeks before expiry; 90 days after expiry to renew; after 90 days a new application with evidence of current course requirements is needed.

Maximum fines: $5,500 for security activity without a Class 1 or 2 licence and for not wearing the licence; $11,000 and/or six months jail for selling or lending a licence; additional conditions breach up to $22,000 corporation or $11,000 and six months individual; sign-on registers each shift; notify change of particulars within 14 days; fee table lists 1, 3 and 5 year terms.

Master licence holders must ensure Class 1 operatives they provide, except 1E, hold a current first aid certificate; no training needed for a Master licence; HLTAID003 and HLTAID006 only accepted if completed before 30 June 2022.

From 5 October 2026, renewing individual operators must complete HLTAID011 Provide First Aid (existing certificate accepted if completed in the three years before expiry) and bodyguards, crowd controllers and security guards must complete the approved refresher within 12 months before renewal; refresher online only, hosted by ASIAL; monitoring centre operator only holders exempt from refresher; renewal application sent 10 weeks before expiry; requirements follow amendments commencing 19 June 2025.

Most changes under the Private Security and County Court Amendment Act 2024 commenced 19 June 2025; all activities licensed; class A and B removed; seven activities defined; ABN contractors need both business and individual licences under section 15A from 19 December 2025 (not investigators); Risk Management Plans under sections 136A and 136B at least one day before the activity.

Training must be with an approved RTO and valid within 12 months of receipt of application; CPP20218 for crowd control, unarmed guard and control room operator; CPP31318 streams for armed guard, cash-in-transit and dog; CPP31418 for bodyguard; CPP30619 for investigator; CPP40719 or approved organisation membership for business licence; no training for installer or adviser; CRICOS condition for student visa holders; prohibited person defined in section 13.
A security guard may be licensed for up to six sub-activities; guard dogs must be trained to the obedience level defined by the Domestic Animals Regulations 2015.
Interstate licence holders apply under mutual recognition for equivalent activities only, not on provisional licences; temporary visitor permits for special events cannot be renewed.

Power to arrest training must be completed before registration (BPC 7583.6 and 7583.8); 32 hours of skills training within six months, with 16 hours within 30 days if certificates cannot be provided; 8 hours annual continuing training (BPC 7583.6, 16 CCR 643); eligibility age 18 (BPC 7582.8); DOJ and FBI check.

Guards keep certificates until registration expires or is canceled; employers keep records for duration of employment; renewal at least 60 days before expiry; registrations not renewed within 60 days of expiration are canceled (BPC 7583.20); web printout allowed pending card (BPC 7583.17).
Pre-registration course is Power to Arrest (3 hours) and Appropriate Use of Force (5 hours) using the DCA manual dated July 2023; in-person topics listed; exam must be passed at 100%.

Two mandatory courses within 30 days of card issue or employment, remaining two four hour mandatory courses within six months; 27 listed electives with maximum hours; annual training 8 hours with a minimum of 2 hours use of force review (BPC 7583.6(e) and 7574.18); four hour baton refresher every other year may count.

16 CCR 643: certificate contents, serially numbered, provider retains certificates at least two years; exam results retained two years or until Bureau inspection; PPO and proprietary employers may train only their direct employees.

Article 25(1) initial, refresher, complementary training; 25(2) theory and practice; 25(4) certified premises and registered trainers; Article 27(1) PSP card valid five years; 27(3) renewal requires refresher course
Article 59(1)(d), (j), (l) very serious offenses; 59(4) legal persons EUR 1,500 to 7,500, 7,500 to 37,500, 15,000 to 44,500; 59(5) individuals EUR 150 to 750, 300 to 1,500, 600 to 3,000

Ordinance 148/2014 Art 4 DNPSP exclusive competence; Art 5 training types; Art 7(3) refresher mandatory on card renewal or where last training over five years ago; Art 9 base module objectives; Art 22 security director course 200 hours minimum at higher education institution

Ordinance 148/2014 Annex II minimum refresher hours: alarm operator 10, vigilante 30, segurança-porteiro 40, close protection 60, sports steward 30, events steward 30, ports and airports 45, cash in transit 55, transport inspector 10

Code: first aiders should hold a nationally recognised Statement of Attainment from an RTO for Provide First Aid or equivalent; additional training examples; CPR refresher annually and qualifications renewed every three years; ratios 1:50 low risk, 1:25 high risk, 1:10 remote high risk; first aid rooms recommended for 200 (low) and 100 (high) workers; five step guide; induction information; first aiders not to exceed training; Regulation 43 emergency plan; mock emergency

Victorian prescribed approach: low risk one first aid officer for 10 to 50, two for 51 to 100, one per additional 100; higher risk one for up to 25, two for 26 to 50, one per additional 50; low risk micro-businesses under 10 employees; Provide First Aid minimum, Provide Advanced First Aid for higher risk; CPR annually and qualifications every three years; at least one officer available during operating times

RSA is required for service staff, food and beverage attendants, retail liquor salespersons, winery and brewery staff, promotional staff, RSA marshals, security staff and crowd controllers, and volunteers; course includes SITHFAB021 plus NSW content.

Competency card valid for five years; multiple endorsements all expire 5 years from the earliest endorsement; 28 day grace period after expiry if identity check completed before expiry; card must be available when working; physical card arrives in 2 to 4 weeks.

In venues with any number of gaming machines, licensees, approved managers, club secretaries, club directors (unless RGBO) and operational hotel company directors must complete ARCG; security officers not recommended as RGOs

Fact sheet: SB 553 amended LC 6401.7; plan may be part of IIPP (section 3203); initial training and annually thereafter; training content list incl. interactive discussions; additional training for new hazards or plan changes; exemptions in subsection (b).
